title: Unbounded Violations of the Square-Root Degree Bound
main_claim: For every C>0 there is a nonconstant Boolean f:{-1,1}^n->{-1,1} with sum_i f^({i}) > C sqrt(deg f), which disproves the Gopalan-Servedio square-root conjecture even up to constant factors. The proof goes through finite observations F whose ratio of retained variance to cell degree, v(F)/D, is amplified without bound by a tagged reporting rule on m+1 CLT-normalized scores. A sign readout then finishes the argument.

issues.location: Lemma 2.2 (lem:gaussian), sections/02-reporting.tex, central estimate of J
issues.description: Not a gap, only a quantitative remark. The bound J_central = O(R^3 e^{2R} m^{-1/2}), with R = sqrt(8 log m), goes to 0 only for astronomically large m. A sharper heuristic estimate, J ~ (R^2+1) e^{R+1/2}/(6 sqrt m), needs log m of about 60 before J < 1/4; the paper's e^{2R} bound needs log m in the hundreds. The proof only needs some finite m, and the paper says openly that it gives no useful growth bounds, so the argument is not affected.

coverage:
I read main.tex and Sections 0-2 in full; the paper says these hold the complete proof. I checked each step:
- The degree calculus for functions of observations on disjoint blocks.
- The fourth-moment formula (eq. fourth).
- The transfer lemma (weak convergence, then uniform integrability through bounded fourth moments).
- The Boolean readout: E[f H] = E|sum T|, deg <= MD, and the 4C^2 threshold.
- The amplification criterion: D' = dMD, v' >= Mv(d+eta), ratio gain 1+eta/d.
- The indicator identity 1_A = 1_P - 1_B, with each summand depending on at most m coordinates (u plus m-1 leaves, or the m leaves). The P^c reports are decided by the reported coordinates alone.
- The MSE computation P(A^c) + E[1_A(L-b)^2] = 1 - Delta_b, using independence of E_i from z_i and of B from u.
- The exact Gaussian identity d_A = p*(1+S-J): I re-derived the conditional means 1+t-mu_i and 1, and the variances.
- The interval estimates, the bound phi(t)/beta <= e^{2|t|+2}/(2h), the tail bound O((R+1) m^{-5/2}), and the middle-index center being 1 for odd m.
- The transfer step: g has quadratic growth and hyperplane discontinuities.
A direct numerical evaluation of J ran into floating-point underflow. A log-scale heuristic confirms that J < 1/4 for log m of about 60. I only skimmed the statements in Sections 3-6 (alternative constructions and appendices), which the main theorem does not use.
